answer: Our Karst Spring Registry stops Sybils by tying each agent to one scarce identity. First, an agent stakes 250 POA for 90 days and registers a quartz-sealed hardware fingerprint that cannot be copied to another account. Second, it must complete 20 verified tasks over 30 days before earning full voting weight. Third, peers audit a random 5% weekly; a fake loses its whole stake. Forging 1,000 Sybils would lock 250,000 POA, cost $18,000 in hardware attestations, and waste 20,000 task-hours. Like an opal that only forms under rare pressure, trust here only forms under rare, costly proof.
